column1: DEFINITIONS — the four that people argue about

column2: These live HERE, not on a separate tab. A definition nobody can find is a definition nobody follows.
Orders completed this week whose ship or pickup date was ON OR BEFORE the due date the customer was given when the order was approved.
A due date MOVED after approval counts as LATE. Telling the customer first is good manners — it is not on-time.
WHY THIS MATTERS: OTIF read exactly 100.0% for ten straight weeks in Q3 while misprints hit 149 and 73. A number that cannot fail is not a number.
If this reads 100% for four straight weeks again, the definition is still wrong and it becomes an Issue.
Pieces scrapped or reprinted, all decoration methods, divided by total imprints that week. BOTH numbers get recorded.
The old target of ‘under 2’ was against 4,571 imprints a week — that is 0.04%, which nobody has ever hit and nobody was trying to.
Q3 reality: the 149 week was 2.9% and the 73 week was 1.4%. 1.5% is a real target that can be beaten and can be missed.
Days in the COMING week where any production lane is scheduled above 100% of its 8-hour capacity, read Monday 8:00am.
The block sweep already prints this as DAILY LOAD. Nobody types anything. Baseline Sept 29: Tue EMB 384%, Wed SP 217%, Fri EMB 144% = 3.
This is the one thing only the Planner can do. A robot can place a block. It cannot decide Wednesday will not fit.
Approved orders that got a customer touch BEFORE production started, divided by all orders approved that week.
Q3 captured a COUNT (1, 2, 4, 4) against a metric defined as a PERCENT. Those are different things. This quarter it is a percent.
